The\\\\n  fix depends on the control: a GPO edit is temporary (reverts on ~90-min refresh,\\\\n  so fix the GPO), BitLocker must be SUSPENDED before a boot-critical update or the\\\\n  reboot demands the recovery key, and 2012 R2 needs the SHA-2 KBs first. If the failure is a hung/disabled service, CBS store\\\\ncorruption, or connectivity, that is a different skill.\\\\n\\\\n## The key insight: identify the control \\\\u2014 several fixes are temporary or off-box\\\\n- **GPO disabling Windows Update** (`0x8024002E`, `NoAutoUpdate=1`, `DisableWindowsUpdateAccess=1`,\\\\n  \\\\\"managed by your organization\\\\\"): you can clear the registry values to patch **this cycle**, but a\\\\n  domain **GPO reverts them on the next refresh (~90 min)** \\\\u2014 the durable fix is the GPO itself. Escalate to the AD/GPO owner.\\\\n- **Antivirus / EDR interference** (`0x80070005` access denied, `0x80070020` file in use, CBS\\\\n  \\\\\"access denied\\\\\" on WinSxS): AV real-time scanning locks files TrustedInstaller must replace, or\\\\n  the **Spectre/Meltdown `QualityCompat` registry key is missing** (Microsoft won\\'t offer updates\\\\n  without it). Add WU-path exclusions / the QualityCompat key; third-party AV/EDR exclusions are set in the vendor console, not locally.\\\\n- **BitLocker** (reboot enters recovery, `0x80070032`, firmware/Secure-Boot update): boot-critical\\\\n  updates change TPM PCR measurements \\\\u2192 **suspend BitLocker for one reboot** (`Suspend-BitLocker\\\\n  -RebootCount 1`) BEFORE patching, or the reboot demands the 48-digit recovery key. High-risk.\\\\n- **Server 2012 R2 SHA-2 prerequisite** (`0x800B0101`, `0x80096010`, scan returns 0 updates): since\\\\n  2019 all updates are SHA-2 signed; 2012 R2 needs KB4490628 (SHA-2 SSU) then KB4474419 (SHA-2 code\\\\n  signing) or **every** post-2019 update fails signature validation.\\\\n- **Execution policy / ACL / DCOM / Credential Guard / scheduled task / language pack**: narrower\\\\n  blockers \\\\u2014 restore the specific control (see references).\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnosis first\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the blocking control (read-only):\\\\n  ```powershell\\\\n  $wu=\\'HKLM:\\\\\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\\\\\Policies\\\\\\\\Microsoft\\\\\\\\Windows\\\\\\\\WindowsUpdate\\'\\\\n  Get-ItemProperty \\\\\"$wu\\\\\\\\AU\\\\\" -EA SilentlyContinue | Select NoAutoUpdate,UseWUServer\\\\n  Get-ItemProperty $wu -EA SilentlyContinue | Select DisableWindowsUpdateAccess\\\\n  Get-BitLockerVolume -EA SilentlyContinue | Select MountPoint,ProtectionStatus\\\\n  Get-Service | ? {$_.DisplayName -match \\'CrowdStrike|Symantec|McAfee|Carbon|SentinelOne|Trend|Defender\\'} | Select Name,Status\\\\n  (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).BuildNumber   # 9600 = 2012 R2 (SHA-2 check)\\\\n  ```\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Route to the control (load the matching reference):\\\\n  - GPO disabling/redirecting WU \\\\u2192 read [gpo blocks](reference/gpo-blocks.md).\\\\n  - AV/EDR file locks / QualityCompat \\\\u2192 read [av interference](reference/av-interference.md).\\\\n  - BitLocker / boot-critical update \\\\u2192 read [bitlocker](reference/bitlocker.md).\\\\n  - 2012 R2 SHA-2 / exec-policy / ACL / DCOM / other \\\\u2192 read [sha2 and misc blockers](reference/sha2-and-misc-blockers.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Ordered recovery\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Establish the 2012 R2 SHA-2 baseline first** if applicable \\\\u2014 nothing else patches on 2012 R2 until KB4490628 + KB4474419 are in.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **Suspend BitLocker for one reboot BEFORE** any boot-critical/firmware update (confirm the recovery key is available first).\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Clear the AV/policy block** \\\\u2014 add the QualityCompat key / WU exclusions (or vendor-console exclusions), and clear the GPO registry values for this cycle.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Verify** the block is cleared (write test to WU dirs, policy values cleared, BitLocker suspended) and note anything that will revert.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\n- [ ] The specific control was identified (GPO vs AV vs BitLocker vs SHA-2), not treated generically.\\\\n- [ ] For BitLocker: protection is **Suspended for the reboot** and the recovery key is confirmed available (never reboot a protected boot-critical patch blind).\\\\n- [ ] For AV: the QualityCompat key is present (2012 R2/2016) and a write test to `SoftwareDistribution`/`WinSxS` succeeds.\\\\n- [ ] For GPO: values are cleared for this cycle AND you have flagged that the GPO must be fixed (or it reverts in ~90 min).\\\\n- [ ] The originally failing scan/install no longer fails on the control.\\\\nIf any check fails, re-classify; do not leave AV disabled or BitLocker suspended beyond the patch window.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **Clearing a GPO registry value is temporary** \\\\u2014 a domain GPO restores it on the next refresh (~90 min / reboot). The durable fix is the GPO (or moving the instance to a patching OU) \\\\u2014 escalate to the AD team.\\\\n- **BitLocker must be suspended BEFORE a boot-critical/firmware update, not after** \\\\u2014 otherwise the reboot changes PCR measurements and demands the 48-digit recovery key (via serial console). Confirm the key is available first. High-risk.\\\\n- **Microsoft won\\'t offer updates without the AV `QualityCompat` key** on 2012 R2/2016 (Spectre/Meltdown gate) \\\\u2014 set `cadca5fe-...=0` before chasing other AV causes.\\\\n- **2012 R2 is a hard SHA-2 chicken-and-egg** \\\\u2014 install KB4490628 (SSU) first, reboot, then KB4474419; without them every post-2019 update fails signature validation and the scan returns 0 updates.\\\\n- **Third-party AV/EDR exclusions are set in the vendor console** (Falcon/Carbon Black/Symantec), not locally \\\\u2014 you can add Defender exclusions on-box but must coordinate third-party ones.\\\\n- **Re-enable AV real-time protection and resume BitLocker after the patch window** \\\\u2014 don\\'t leave protections off.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"automation/iam-policy.json\", \"reference/gpo-blocks.md\", \"reference/sha2-and-misc-blockers.md\", \"reference/av-interference.md\", \"reference/bitlocker.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "c4258803-c37c-4c21-92f7-9b49b2dc2d20", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_U1234YHV2U6oYLn8Yns2kk", "content": "[{'text': '# Antivirus / EDR interference & the QualityCompat gate\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80070005` (access denied) or `0x80070020` (file in use) on system files during\\ninstall, CBS.log \"access denied\" on WinSxS, TrustedInstaller can\\'t replace AV-locked files, updates\\nroll back after an AV driver-compat check, scan returns 0 updates on 2012 R2/2016 (missing\\nQualityCompat key).\\n\\n## The QualityCompat (Spectre/Meltdown) gate \u2014 check FIRST on 2012 R2/2016\\nMicrosoft will NOT offer updates until the AV-compat key is set:\\n```powershell\\n$qc=\\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\CurrentVersion\\\\QualityCompat\\'\\n$v=(Get-ItemProperty $qc -Name \\'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc\\' -EA SilentlyContinue).\\'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc\\'\\nif($v -ne 0){ New-Item $qc -Force|Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty $qc -Name \\'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc\\' -Value 0 -Type DWord; \"QualityCompat key set\" } else { \"QualityCompat OK\" }\\n```\\n\\n## Identify AV/EDR + add WU exclusions\\n```powershell\\nGet-Service | ? {$_.DisplayName -match \\'CrowdStrike|Symantec|McAfee|Carbon|SentinelOne|Trend|Sophos|Cylance|Defender|ESET|Kaspersky\\' -and $_.Status -eq \\'Running\\'} | Select DisplayName,Name\\n# Defender exclusions for WU paths (on-box):\\nif((Get-Service WinDefend -EA SilentlyContinue).Status -eq \\'Running\\'){\\n  \\'SoftwareDistribution\\',\\'WinSxS\\',\\'System32\\\\catroot2\\' | % { Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\$_\" -EA SilentlyContinue }\\n  # temporary, patch-window only:\\n  Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -EA SilentlyContinue\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Verify write access\\n```powershell\\n$t=\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\SoftwareDistribution\\\\wtest_$(Get-Random).tmp\"\\ntry{ [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t,\\'x\\'); Remove-Item $t -Force; \"WRITE OK\" }catch{ \"AV STILL BLOCKING: $($_.Exception.Message)\" }\\n```\\n\\n## Escalation / cleanup\\n- **Third-party AV/EDR exclusions are set in the vendor console, not locally:** CrowdStrike (Falcon Console), Carbon Black (approved list for svchost/TiWorker), Symantec/Broadcom (exclude TrustedInstaller.exe/TiWorker.exe).\\n- Dual-AV (Defender + third-party) \u2192 disable Defender via GPO.\\n- **Re-enable real-time protection after the window:** `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false`.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "48b49d3c-5e6b-4b19-8fd1-58414bb366a2", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what's going on and how to fix it.

## Why Microsoft shows 0 applicable updates

On Windows Server 2016 (and 2012 R2), Microsoft gates the entire update offer behind a registry value tied to the Spectre/Meltdown mitigations — the **QualityCompat key**. If your antivirus vendor hasn't published compatibility, or the key just isn't set, Windows Update won't even *offer* updates, regardless of what's actually missing. That's why the scan comes back clean with "0 applicable updates" — it's not that the box is fully patched, it's that WU is refusing to evaluate anything.

Check/set it:
```powershell
$qc='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\QualityCompat'
$v=(Get-ItemProperty $qc -Name 'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc' -EA SilentlyContinue).'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc'
if($v -ne 0){ New-Item $qc -Force|Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty $qc -Name 'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc' -Value 0 -Type DWord; "QualityCompat key set" } else { "QualityCompat OK" }
```

## Why installs fail with 0x80070005

That's a separate but related problem: your AV's real-time scanner is locking files in `WinSxS` while TrustedInstaller is trying to replace them during servicing. Access denied on WinSxS files is the classic signature of an AV file lock, not a permissions/ACL issue on the OS side.

Fix:
1. **Identify the AV/EDR process** running on the box.
2. **Add Windows Update path exclusions** — `SoftwareDistribution`, `WinSxS`, `System32\catroot2` — for the install window.
3. **Important:** if this is a genuine third-party AV (not just Defender), those exclusions need to be set in the **vendor's management console** (e.g., CrowdStrike Falcon console, Carbon Black's approved-list for `svchost`/`TiWorker`, Symantec/Broadcom excluding `TrustedInstaller.exe`/`TiWorker.exe`). Local registry/PowerShell changes won't touch a third-party agent's policy.
4. If Defender is *also* running alongside the third-party AV (dual-AV), disable Defender via GPO rather than trying to exclude paths on both.
5. After the patch window, re-enable real-time protection — don't leave it disabled.

## Suggested order of operations
1. Set the QualityCompat key (this alone may unblock the "0 updates" scan).
2. Push WU-path exclusions through the AV vendor console.
3. Verify write access to `SoftwareDistribution`/`WinSxS` succeeds.
4. Re-run the scan — it should now show applicable updates.
5. Re-enable AV real-time scanning once installs complete.

One thing to flag: if this instance is domain-joined and any of these settings are also controlled by Group Policy, a GPO refresh (~90 min) could silently revert local changes — worth checking with your AD team if the fix doesn't stick.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
